discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: The nominees turned ultracold atoms in optical lattices into programmable quantum matter that answers questions from condensed-matter physics by direct measurement. Bloch and Greiner observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition of bosons (2002), which established lattice gases as clean realisations of Hubbard models. Esslinger extended this to fermions, imaging Fermi surfaces in 3D lattices and, with Bloch independently, observing the fermionic Mott insulator (2008), a first step toward simulating high-temperature superconductivity. Greiner and Bloch then invented quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution. These made it possible to see antiferromagnetic correlations, string order and entanglement directly, and they led to today's neutral-atom quantum processors. Their techniques are now standard in hundreds of laboratories. They created a new experimental paradigm, analogue quantum simulation, which connects atomic physics, condensed matter and quantum information.
